title: Call surface normalizer with mapping backfill for legacy function compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
OpenAI-style tool calling (name + JSON schema + deterministic invocation signal) and our older "legacy functions" surface (ad-hoc signatures, positional args, ad-hoc naming conventions) are being used concurrently by customers. This creates failures in multi-model routing, tool-call fallbacks, and streaming scenarios when the runtime must match a request to an available tool/function.

Goal:
Provide a runtime-level call surface normalizer that: 1) produces a canonical identifier for tools/functions across OpenAI-style and legacy surfaces, 2) supports a mapping backfill process to gradually align legacy function names and deprecated parameter shapes without forcing customers to change code immediately, and 3) preserves streaming behavior and structured output semantics for tool invocations.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: canonical name registry, fuzzy and heuristics-based name matching, mapping backfill job, provenance headers in runtime logs, metrics for ambiguous matches, shim adapter that transforms legacy call payloads to current tool schemas, minimal API surface to opt-out.
- Out-of-scope: breaking changes to public SDK call semantics, wholesale customer migrations, UI for editing mappings (follow-up ticket).

Design overview:
1) Canonical registry: maintain an in-memory and persisted mapping of canonical_tool_id -> {aliases: [strings], schema_hash, last_seen_version}. The registry is loaded at runtime and exposed to the router for name resolution. Persisted store is in our config DB (encrypted).
2) Normalization pipeline: incoming call metadata flows through a Normalizer that: lowercases and trims candidate names, applies character folding (snake/camel/kebab), consults exact alias map, then runs a deterministic fuzzy match (trigram similarity + schema-shape heuristics). Matches emit a confidence score.
3) Backfill job: periodic worker that scans call telemetry, finds high-confidence alias candidates not in registry, groups suggestions and auto-promotes mappings once usage crosses thresholds (e.g., 100 calls with confidence > 0.85 over 7 days). Low-confidence suggestions surface to ops as review items.
4) Legacy adapter: at runtime, when a legacy function signature is identified, the adapter applies parameter renames and positional->named translation using best-effort heuristics and a small transformation DSL. Adapter emits structured warnings in response metadata for customers to see.
5) Streaming considerations: tool-call events can arrive mid-stream (streamed function call initiation and streaming tool outputs). The Normalizer must resolve names deterministically on first event and annotate subsequent streamed chunks with the canonical_tool_id to prevent re-resolution. If resolution occurs late (after partial stream), the runtime will insert a canonical-id synthetic event and mark earlier chunks with provisional=true.
6) Fallback policy: if multiple high-confidence matches exist, prefer exact alias match -> schema_hash match -> higher recent-usage timestamp -> customer-specified preference. If ambiguous and confidence < 0.6, route to configured fallback model/variant.

Trade-offs considered:
- Heuristic matching reduces customer friction but risks false positives. We bias for precision (higher confidence threshold) and log ambiguity for operator review.
- Persisted registry simplifies cluster restarts but adds a write path that needs RBAC and audit logging (security review).
- Auto-promote backfill improves velocity but requires careful thresholds to avoid silent breaking changes; we default to conservative thresholds and require ops opt-in for auto-promote in enterprise tenants.

Acceptance criteria (must pass):
- The normalizer resolves >95% of canonical matches for a curated set of 200 mixed legacy/OpenAI tool name examples without false-positive mapping rate >1%.
- Backfill job suggests mappings and auto-promotes per thresholds in a staging tenant; suggestions surfaced in ops dashboard.
- Streaming function call tests preserve ordering and the runtime emits canonical_tool_id in first resolved event. Edge-case where resolution occurs late should emit synthetic canonical event and not duplicate final tool outputs.
- Metrics emitted: normalized_matches, ambiguous_match_rate, auto_promote_count, legacy_adapter_transform_rate, mapping_suggestion_count.
- Security review completed and persisted registry reads/writes audited.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: RFC + schema for canonical registry, decide persisted store schema and RBAC. (PR: draft link in docs).
- Week 2: Implement Normalizer (in-memory) and deterministic fuzzy matcher; unit tests and offline simulation against call logs.
- Week 3: Implement adapter transformation DSL and streaming integration hooks; integration tests with stream harness.
- Week 4: Implement backfill worker and ops suggestion API; wire metrics.
- Week 5: Staging rollout, canary on 5% of traffic for non-enterprise tenants, observe metrics and guard rails.
- Week 6: Enterprise opt-in policy and documentation.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for matcher determinism and schema-shape heuristics.
- End-to-end tests: simulate OpenAI tool call, legacy function call, ambiguous name collisions, and streaming-first-event-late scenarios.
- Load tests for Normalizer at 10k req/s to validate latency budget (<1ms added to routing path).
- Security pen-test on persisted registry write path.

Rollout and monitoring:
- Canary stage with feature flag per-organization. Monitor ambiguous_match_rate and error budgets. Auto-promote disabled by default for orgs with >P2 support flags.
- Post-rollout 30-day review to assess mapping accuracy and customer support tickets.

Links and artifacts:
- RFC draft: https://confluence.redwood/compat/call-surface-normalizer (internal)
- Simulation dataset: gs://redwood-simulations/toolname-mix-2025-01
- Streaming harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287 (WIP)

- Follow-up ticket will add a Console UI for ops to approve/reject backfill suggestions and manually edit alias lists.
